questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A door of mass $M$ and width $L$ is hinged at one end and rotates about a vertical axis without friction. A bullet of mass $m(m \ll M)$ fired perpendicularly to the door at a speed $v$ gets embedded in it at a distance $x$ from its axis of rotation. Assuming the door was stationary initially, how does the resultant angular speed $\omega$ of the door vary as a function of $x$ ?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The position of a particle of mass 1 kg at time $t$ is given by $\mathbf{r} = t\,\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 2t^2\,\hat{k}$, where $t$ is in seconds and the coefficients have the proper units for $\mathbf{r}$ to be in metres. What is the component of the angular momentum (with respect to the origin) in kg m^2$ s^{-1}$ along the vector $(\hat{i} + \hat{j})$?
questions.solution:
The position vector of the particle is given by $\vec{r} = t\,\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 2t^2\,\hat{k}$.

The velocity vector is the time derivative of the position vector:
$\vec{v} = \dfrac{d\vec{r}}{dt} = \hat{i} + 4t\,\hat{k}$

The linear momentum of the particle is:
$\vec{p} = m\vec{v} = 1 \times (\hat{i} + 4t\,\hat{k}) = \hat{i} + 4t\,\hat{k}$

The angular momentum $\vec{L}$ with respect to the origin is given by $\vec{r} \times \vec{p}$:
$\vec{L} = (t\,\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 2t^2\,\hat{k}) \times (\hat{i} + 4t\,\hat{k})$

Evaluating the cross product:
$\vec{L} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} \text{ and } \hat{j} \text{ and } \hat{k} \\ t \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 2t^2 \\ 1 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 4t \end{vmatrix}$

$\vec{L} = \hat{i}(1 \times 4t - 0) - \hat{j}(t \times 4t - 2t^2 \times 1) + \hat{k}(0 - 1 \times 1)$
$\vec{L} = 4t\,\hat{i} - 2t^2\,\hat{j} - \hat{k}$

We need the component of $\vec{L}$ along the vector $\vec{A} = \hat{i} + \hat{j}$. The unit vector along $\vec{A}$ is:
$\hat{u} = \dfrac{\hat{i} + \hat{j}}{\sqrt{1^2 + 1^2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\hat{i} + \hat{j})$

The component of the angular momentum along this direction is the dot product $\vec{L} \cdot \hat{u}$:
$\vec{L} \cdot \hat{u} = (4t\,\hat{i} - 2t^2\,\hat{j} - \hat{k}) \cdot \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\hat{i} + \hat{j})$

$\vec{L} \cdot \hat{u} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(4t \times 1 - 2t^2 \times 1 - 1 \times 0) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(4t - 2t^2)$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(4t - 2t^2)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A circular disk of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is rotating clockwise with a uniform angular velocity $\omega$ about an axis passing through the centre, normal to the disk. At time $t=0$, a torque $T$ is applied along the same axis to oppose the rotation of the disk. What is the angular displacement $\theta$ (measured from $t=0$ in the clockwise direction) that the disk attains before it starts rotating counterclockwise?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An inextensible cord of negligible mass passes over the rim of a solid disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$. The disc is free to rotate about an axis passing through the centre perpendicular to the plane of the screen, as shown in the figure. Two blocks of masses $M$ and $M / 2$ are attached to the two free ends of the cord. Assume that there is no slipping of the cord on the disc. The acceleration due to gravity is $g$. What is the value of the angular acceleration of the disc?
